Trace the calibration curve over a grid of interventions

Source: R/calibration-curve.R
calibration_curve.Rd

For each intervention alpha in alpha_grid on the intensity of the process z_name, estimates the risk of z_name (the exposure) and of each target under that intervention. Plotting the target estimates against the exposure estimates traces out the calibration curve relating the two. The standard errors of the target estimates account for calibrating to the estimated exposure risk rather than to alpha.

Usage

calibration_curve(
  initial_fit,
  target,
  z_name = "z",
  alpha_grid = seq(0, 5, length.out = 10),
  a = NULL,
  min_iter = 1,
  target_by_state = FALSE,
  block_size_z = NULL,
  block_size_target = NULL,
  cores = 1,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

initial_fit

An initial fit, as returned by fit_initial().

target

Character vector. Names of the processes whose risks are estimated.

z_name

String. Name of the process whose intensity alpha scales. If no such process exists in initial_fit, alpha is ignored with a warning.

alpha_grid

Non-negative numeric vector. The interventions to evaluate.

a

Optional baseline treatment value (0 or 1) to intervene on. Must be one of the values of a given to fit_initial().

min_iter

Non-negative integer. Minimum number of TMLE iterations, passed on to tmle_alpha().

target_by_state

Logical. If TRUE, use state-specific clever covariates in the targeting step.

block_size_z, block_size_target

Optional positive integers. If given, the expected time lost is estimated for z_name and target, respectively, instead of the risk; see years_lost in tmle_alpha().

cores

Positive integer. Number of cores used by parallel::mclapply() for the per-individual computations.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, print progress.

...

Further arguments passed on to tmle_alpha().

Value

A list with elements:

  • estimate: a data.table with one row per value of alpha_grid and columns alpha, exposure_est, exposure_se, target_est and target_se (suffixed by _<target> when there are several targets).

  • checks: per value of alpha_grid, the estimated derivatives of the exposure and target estimates with respect to alpha.

  • eics: per value of alpha_grid, the influence curves alpha_eic, calibration_eic, target_eic and eic.

Examples

fit <- fit_initial(
  illness_death,
  fit_types = list(
    z = list(
      delta = 2,
      model = ~ L0,
      at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0
    ),
    death = list(delta = 1, model = ~ L0 + z),
    censoring = list(delta = 0, model = ~ L0)
  ),
  tau = 1
)

curve <- calibration_curve(
  fit,
  target = "death",
  z_name = "z",
  alpha_grid = c(0, 0.5, 1)
)
curve$estimate
#>    alpha exposure_est exposure_se target_est  target_se
#>    <num>        <num>       <num>      <num>      <num>
#> 1:   0.0   0.00000000  0.00000000  0.2820265 0.03975707
#> 2:   0.5   0.08791201  0.01791587  0.3040549 0.03896630
#> 3:   1.0   0.16448600  0.03131500  0.3239449 0.03949105
